question.text: For a reaction taking place in three steps at same temperature, overall rate constant <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mfrac></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Ea</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Ea</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Ea</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math> respectively, the overall <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ea</mi></math> is _________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kJ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>mol</mi></math>.

solution.text:
According to Arrhenius concept,

K=Ae-Ea/RT

Given that,

K=K1.K2/K3

Using Arrhenius equation we can expand above equation as

e-Ea(net)/RT=e-Ea1/RT×e-Ea2/RTe-Ea3/RT

Hence,

 Ea(net)=Ea1+Ea2-Ea3⇒Ea(net)=40+50-60=30kJ/mol
